summary.headline: HCG Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 7,318 million, while EBITDA margin expanded to 19.7%, but trade margin caps on oncology drugs bring a mid-to-high single-digit annualized EBITDA hit.
summary.overview: HCG reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 7,318 million (+16% YoY, +14% excluding North Bengaluru), driven by 9% patient volume growth and 7% ARPP growth, with EBITDA of INR 1,425 million (+17%) and margin of 19.7% versus 19.2%. Management said a roughly INR 60 million Karnataka wage revision weighed on margins; like-for-like EBITDA growth was above 20%. H1 FY27 consolidated revenue was INR 14,100 million (+15%) and adjusted EBITDA INR 2,740 million (+18%). The main new overhang is the trade margin cap on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, effective November, which management estimates at a mid-to-high single-digit percentage of annualized EBITDA. Figures exclude the divested Milann Fertility business.

segments.name: South cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,941 million (+18%, 40% of total), with ARPP +14% and patient volumes +4%, aided by Bengaluru CoE and North Bengaluru ramp-up.

segments.name: West cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 3,147 million (+10%, 43% of total), volumes +7% and ARPP +3%; Maharashtra grew mid-teens while Gujarat was moderated by deliberate cuts to low-margin institutional business.

segments.name: East cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 928 million (+23%, 11% of total), volumes +18% and ARPP +5%, led by Ranchi.

segments.name: Kenya (international)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 302 million (about +54% YoY), supported by a new radiation machine and 13 new medical oncology beds.

segments.name: Non-institutional business
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 21% YoY and rose to 69% of revenue share (over 300 bps gain); institutional growth was 5%.

segments.name: North Bengaluru (new hospital)
segments.commentary: Q2 EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 61 million from about INR 75 million in Q1; monthly EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Trade margin cap on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs: mid-to-high single-digit % annualized EBITDA impact; for H2 FY27 management indicated a proportionately lower, low-mid single-digit impact, with impact from Q3 (effective November).
Management says FY28 onwards there should be no material impact and the company should catch up on margins.

Medium-term guidance reiterated: mid-teens revenue growth with high-teens to 20% EBITDA growth; FY28-FY29 trajectory of mid-teens revenue growth and high-teens EBITDA growth with continued margin improvement.
ARPP growth guided at least ahead of inflation.
North Bengaluru to reach monthly EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27 (January-March 2027).
Gujarat expected to return to mid-teens growth by Q4 FY27.
Near-term effective tax rate of about 30-35%, expected to stabilise after roughly a year.
No further material EPCG provisions expected near term; no cash impact so far.
capex_capacity: Added 25 operational beds in Q2 (13 Kenya, 7 Kolkata, 5 Nagpur); 146 beds operationalised in H1 FY27.
MR-LINAC adaptive radiation therapy system operationalised at North Bengaluru hospital.
Cardiac surgical robotic system added at multi-specialty hospital in Ahmedabad; new radiation therapy machine added in Kenya.
H1 FY27 capex INR 1,279 million for capacity expansion, medical equipment and infrastructure upgrades.
Acquired additional 34% stake in Vizag operations (MG Vizag) for about INR 150-160 crore, funded from rights issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Patient volumes +9% and ARPP +7% in Q2; robotic surgeries +37% YoY, with high-end radiation, theranostics and favourable payor mix driving ARPP.
Management says the payor mix shift applies to cash, insurance and corporate, and that some institutional volumes (notably Gujarat) will be moderated deliberately.
MVT (medical value travel) business growing about 25%; expected at 4-5% of overall revenue in H1 FY27 versus about 3% in the prior year.
Trade margin cap covers 137 drugs; management said nearly all oncology drugs now sit under the 30% cap, with immunotherapy already below it.

qa_highlights.question: How to estimate the EBITDA impact of the trade margin cap on 137 drugs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined granular math, saying the impact is mid-to-high single-digit % annualized, offset by trade channel optimisation, volume growth, utilisation and operating levers. Detail deferred offline.

qa_highlights.question: Size of the EPCG provision and any cash impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Exceptional provision of INR 116 million after a full review of export obligations; no further material provisions expected near term and no cash impact so far.

qa_highlights.question: When will North Bengaluru break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27 (Jan-Mar 2027); losses narrowed from about INR 7.5 crore in Q1 to about INR 6 crore in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 operating cash flow weak (CFO/EBITDA about 54%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to about INR 35 crore Aarogyasri receipts shown as borrowings, a roughly 30-day rise in one major supplier's credit period, and a tax expense of about INR 30 crore versus a INR 99.6 crore deferred tax asset recognised last year. Conversion expected to normalise to 80-85%.

qa_highlights.question: Use of rights issue proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 150 crore for the MG Vizag acquisition, INR 170 crore for debt repayment, and INR 100 crore for general corporate purposes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the tax rate for FY27 and beyond still reasonable?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term effective tax rate of about 30-35%, stabilising to a similar range after about a year.

risks_watch: Trade margin cap effective November 2026: monitor Q3 margin impact versus the mid-to-high single-digit annualized estimate; management would not give detailed drug-level math.
Karnataka wage revision adding about INR 60 million per quarter in employee costs.
Gujarat and institutional business moderation could weigh on West cluster growth until Q4 FY27.
Operating cash flow conversion fell to about 54% in H1; watch for normalisation to 80-85% and any further supplier credit-period changes.
North Bengaluru monthly EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27 is a key milestone.
Geopolitical disruption (Middle East, Bangladesh) affecting export-linked projections; EPCG retrospective exposure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume, ARPP and guidance, with management reiterating mid-teens revenue and high-teens EBITDA growth. Noticeably evasive and brief on the trade margin cap's quantum and drug-level math, and on the regulatory outlook (independent regulator "no idea").
key_quotes: Based on our assessment on an absolute basis, we estimate a mid-to-high single-digit percentage impact to EBITDA on an annualized basis.
The impact, whatever impact we see will be only seen from Q3 onwards, because this is effective November.
I do not think there will be any impact.
I do not think there will be a material impact, honestly, FY 2028 onwards, and we should be able to catch up.

growth.why: Management reaffirmed mid-teens revenue growth with high-teens EBITDA growth for FY28-29 (guidance held), backed by 146 beds operationalised in H1, new equipment, North Bengaluru ramp and 6-9% volume and ARPP gains, though no specific forward capacity pipeline with numbers was given and trade margin caps weigh on EBITDA.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Trade margin cap on 137 anti-cancer drugs from November carries a mid-to-high single-digit % annualized EBITDA hit (low-mid single-digit in H2 FY27), offset by H1 margin of 19.7% vs 18.8% and North Bengaluru losses narrowing from ~INR 75m to INR 61m; management says no material impact from FY28 and margin catch-up.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 146 beds operationalised in H1 FY27 with 25 more in Q2 and North Bengaluru ramping to monthly EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27, but no forward bed or plant pipeline with numbers was given, so the signal is mainly ramp-up of existing capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Patient volumes grew 9% in Q2 and robotic surgeries +37%, MVT growing ~25%, and East volumes +18%, though Gujarat institutional volumes are deliberately being moderated and West volumes were only +7%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: H1 FY27 capex was INR 1,279m and the company bought an extra 34% in MG Vizag for INR 150-160 crore, but no new capex plan or utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed mid-teens revenue and high-teens EBITDA growth for FY28-29 rather than raising it, and the trade margin cap is a new headwind.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Trade margin cap hits from Q3 (mid-to-high single-digit % annualized EBITDA), Karnataka wage revision adds ~INR 60m per quarter, and operating cash conversion fell to ~54% in H1 (target 80-85%); drug-level math was not given.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launches were discussed; only equipment additions such as MR-LINAC, cardiac robotics and a Kenya radiation machine.

rows.label: Trade margin cap on 137 anti-cancer drugs
rows.why: Effective November 2026 with mid-to-high single-digit % annualized EBITDA impact, lower at low-mid single-digit in H2 FY27; management says no material impact from FY28 and the company should catch up on margins.

rows.label: North Bengaluru monthly EBITDA breakeven
rows.why: Q2 loss narrowed to INR 61m from ~INR 75m in Q1, and management says it is set to hit monthly breakeven in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Operating cash conversion normalisation
rows.why: H1 FY27 CFO was about 54% of EBITDA versus 80%+ in H1 FY26; management expects a return to 80-85%, citing Aarogyasri receipts (~INR 35 crore) and a ~30-day rise in one supplier's credit period.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume, ARPP and reiterated mid-teens revenue and high-teens EBITDA growth; it was evasive on the trade margin cap's quantum and drug-level math, and analysts pushed on the cap's EBITDA impact and the regulatory outlook.
